rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions`.

The requirement has two parts. The description MUST say when to use the skill in terms of the user's task. It MAY name another bundled skill where the two could be confused.

The front-matter `description` meets the MUST. It says to use the skill before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a Habeas project. It adds "even when the user only asks for a feature, bug fix, CLI flag, test, dependency bump, or wording tweak". It also says to use it when writing or revising reference chapters. These are all user tasks. The later text on what the skill does (drafting, review, adding references) is extra detail and does not break the requirement.

It names `habeas-refactor` and `habeas-evidence` to separate the skills from each other. The requirement allows this with MAY, so it is not a gap.

The requirement lists no violation queries, so there is no match to judge.
